title: Hyperemic Myocardial Blood Flow Quantification with CZT-based SPECT Cameras
author: Yu-Hua Fang
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.iqjcdun

steps.title: Inject resting tracer
steps.instruction: Inject the subject intravenously with 10 mCi of 99mTc‑Sestamibi as a bolus under resting conditions.

steps.title: Allow tracer uptake
steps.instruction: Wait 60 minutes to allow tracer uptake before imaging.

steps.title: Position subject on scanner
steps.instruction: Place the subject on the scanner table and adjust the position via scintigraphy so that the heart is centered in the field of view.

steps.title: Start list‑mode acquisition
steps.instruction: Initiate list‑mode data acquisition and continue recording for 24 minutes.

steps.title: Administer dipyridamole stress
steps.instruction: After 5 minutes of scanning, start a dipyridamole infusion at 0.142 mg kg⁻¹ min⁻¹, delivering the drug slowly over 4 minutes.

steps.title: Inject stress tracer
steps.instruction: Five minutes after the dipyridamole infusion ends, inject 20 mCi of 99mTc‑Sestamibi intravenously as a bolus.

steps.title: Terminate scan
steps.instruction: Stop the scan 10 minutes after the second tracer injection.

steps.title: Process resting TAC
steps.instruction: Draw a region of interest (ROI), obtain its time‑activity curve (TAC), calculate the mean activity of the first 5 minutes (resting phase), and subtract this mean from the entire TAC to remove residual resting activity.

steps.title: Derive input function
steps.instruction: Draw an ROI in the left ventricular (LV) cavity on a short‑axis slice, then subtract the residual activity of the rest acquisition from that of the stress acquisition to generate the input function for kinetic modeling.

steps.title: Fit kinetic model
steps.instruction: Fit the tissue stress TACs for the LV and myocardium with a two‑tissue‑compartment model using the LV TACs as input functions in COMKAT software; use the estimated kinetic rate constant K1 to approximate hyperemic myocardial blood flow (MBF).
